lines.text: Time for K-Culture. And I'm told someone here is very excited. Offbeat, our K-pop and entertainment desk.
I'm not excited. I'm calm. I'm so calm. FIN.K.L IS BACK!
There it is.
Offbeat, you've been vibrating since this morning.
That's not vibrating. That's my heart doing choreography.
Medically speaking, he's fine. Emotionally, he's a disaster.
I made a vision board. It's just the word "FIN.K.L" in twelve fonts.
Is that a vision?
It's a lifestyle.
For viewers who didn't grow up in the nineties: who is Fin.K.L?
First-generation K-pop royalty. A four-member girl group that debuted in 1998. Their big rival back then was S.E.S.
Nineteen ninety-eight. So, K-pop before it went global?
Back when "going viral" meant staying home with a cold.
And "streaming" meant a leaky pipe.
Back when your phone flipped open, and your whole personality lived on a website called Cyworld.
I had a MySpace page. It was a crime scene.
Let's meet them. Starting with Lee Hyori.
Lee Hyori went solo and became one of Korea's biggest stars, and a variety-show favorite too.
Next, Ock Joo-hyun.
She became one of Korea's top musical theater stars.
Singing and acting live, every night. I can barely finish one shift.
Lee Jin?
Lee Jin moved into acting.
And Sung Yuri.
Sung Yuri became a drama lead, in hits like "Romance Town" and "Feast of the Gods."
One pop queen, one stage star, two actresses. Four careers, one group chat.
Skills: singing, acting, dancing, and surviving a camper van.
Weakness: none. Hobbies: none. Fear: Wi-Fi.
Now the news. On September twenty-first, their agency announced that all four members will return as a group.
Four members. One agency. Zero spoilers.
Wait. When was the last time all four did something together?
The last full-group release was a digital single in 2005. It was called "Forever Fin.K.L." After that, the group went quiet.
Forever lasted twenty-one years. That's one damn long intermission.
Somebody born in 2005 is now twenty-one.
Old enough to vote, drink, and be disappointed by group projects.
And a fan who was fourteen in 2005 is thirty-five now. They have jobs. And credit cards.
Oh no. That's the real news.
They did get together in 2019, right?
A TV show called "Camping Club." They made music for it. But that was a one-off, built around a broadcast.
What was the show about?
Four old friends, one camper van, a road trip around Korea. They talked about life after the group, and whether to perform together again for their twenty-first anniversary.
A road trip with a very big question in the glove box.
It premiered in July 2019 to strong ratings. People loved it.
So, a high school reunion. With cameras. And tents.
This time is different. Their agency says no one-off. About two years of meeting fans, with music, performances, and more.
More, meaning what?
Documentaries, variety shows, exhibitions, official merchandise, brand collabs, ads, and fan projects.
Translation: there will be a mug. And damn right I'm buying the mug.
Nobody's buying just one mug.
They'll buy the mug, a second mug, and the mug's cousin.
The mug has a cousin?
Everything has a cousin. It's called a limited edition.
Let's pitch some documentary titles.
"Fin.K.L: The Sequel."
"Fast and Fin.K.L."
"Fin.K.L and the Temple of Doom."
"Fin.K.L Two: Electric Boogaloo."
Please stop. That is not how any of this works.
I wrote a fanfic about it!
...Of course you did.
It's four hundred pages. It has a prologue. And a map.
A map?!
Fandom lore needs geography, Doctor.
Offbeat, you used to train to be an idol, right?
I was this close to debuting.
How close?
Close enough to know a practice room smells like sweat and ambition.
And you were half a beat late.
Half a beat. Every time.
Okay. Let's play Reunion Bingo.
Free space: somebody cries. Everybody cries.
Square two: somebody says, "We never really left."
Square three: a brand announces a collab within the hour.
Square four: a coworker says, "My mom loves them."
Bingo. I won a game I didn't know I was playing.
Why does this matter outside Korea?
Because it shows how Korean fandom works. Fans don't just grow up with a group. They grow old with a group. In a very loud, glowing way.
Glowing?
Light sticks. Every group has an official one. Thousands of them in the dark look like a galaxy that bought merch.
In America, we get nostalgia tours. A guy in a leather jacket, a lot of knees.
Knees?
Doctor's observation. Reunion tours are mostly knees.
Not these knees. These knees have a choreographer.
Fun fact?
The name stands for "Fine Killing Liability." [VERIFY]
Sounds like a law firm.
A very stylish law firm.
Anyway. The comeback is real. I'm calm. I'm calm!
He is not calm.
Which group would you bring back? Tell us in the comments.

segments.headline: October: a new K-pop release every day
segments.hook: October: a new K-pop release every day

lines.text: Next, the K-pop calendar. Because in October, it's a lot.
I made a spreadsheet. It has colors. It has tabs. It has a tab for the tabs.
Doctor's note: very healthy hobby. I'm proud of the tabs.
Quick vocabulary check. In K-pop, what does "comeback" mean?
A new release. New music, new concept, new promotions.
So you can come back without ever leaving?
That's the best part. You can come back on Monday, and again in March.
In America, a comeback means you disappeared for ten years and a reality show saved you.
So how many new releases this month?
One tracker lists fifty-two scheduled for October. Albums, mini albums, EPs, from groups and solo artists.
Fifty-two? October has thirty-one days.
So that's more than one new release every single day.
I have fewer appointments than that. And I'm a doctor.
Okay, let's go. This week, according to that tracker. October sixth: KickFlip, X:IN, and Yesung.
X:IN. Is that a band or a Wi-Fi password?
October seventh: ONEW and ZICO team up. The song is called "Tic Tac Toe."
Finally, a K-pop song I can play on a napkin.
ONEW is from SHINee, one of K-pop's veteran boy groups. ZICO is a rapper and producer who started in Block B.
A singer and a rapper. Is this a duet or a negotiation?
Two seasoned pros. I trained for years in a practice room. They actually debuted.
October eighth: N.Flying, plus YUQI of i-dle with a mini album called "27."
Just "27"? The whole title is a number?
That's it. Minimalism.
I respect a short title. Like my patients' attention span.
Quick K-pop culture question. Why do idols get photographed just for walking into an airport?
Because airport fashion is a thing. Photographers wait there, and the walk becomes a runway.
I walk through airports all the time. Nobody photographs me.
Give it time.
Next week. October twelfth: Sung Han-bin of ZEROBASEONE makes his solo debut with an EP called "DEAD:ALIVE."
Dead or alive? That's not a title. That's a triage question.
K-pop idols also learn heart signs. Finger heart, arm heart, big heart.
I know one heart. The anatomical one.
Also on the twelfth: Xdinary Heroes with "IMPULSE."
And near the end of the month, October twenty-third: LISA of BLACKPINK with "PRESS PLAY."
Finally, a title that's also an instruction.
October twenty-sixth: ILLIT with "BREAK EVEN," and IVE with "Looks Can Kill."
"Break Even." The only financial goal my clinic has ever hit.
ILLIT is one of K-pop's newer groups. They debuted in 2024. [VERIFY]
And "Looks Can Kill" is basically a warning label. I'll sign the waiver.
And IVE is going full superhero movie. Six members, six hero names: Captain Purple, Wonder Green, Jean Yellow, Bat Pink, Super Blue, Spider Red.
Bat Pink. I'd read that comic.
Pre-release is October nineteenth. The album comes out October twenty-sixth.
And it's a close race! IVE on the inside, LISA coming up fast on the outside!
Please stop commentating.
I can't. It's live.
Offbeat, how do fans survive fifty-two releases?
Simple. You stream. You vote. You buy the album. Then you buy the other version of the album.
The same album? Again?
Different cover. Different photocard. It's called collecting.
So that's where the mug's cousin comes from.
The mug's cousin has a photocard.
Damn. I knew it.
Fun fact: if you listened to one release a day, October would take you nearly two months.
That's without sleeping. Or repeats.
Repeats are mandatory. That's the whole point.
Who's your pick of the month?
I can't choose. I love them all equally. Ask me again after I've heard them.
Tell us your pick in the comments. And please tell Offbeat to drink water.
I'm calm. I'm hydrated. I'm calm!
That was K-Culture. Thanks for watching.
I'm calm.
He is holding a light stick in each hand.
That's the show. Subscribe, and we'll see you next week.
Bye! Drink water! I'm calm!
Stay curious. Keep your lenses clean.
